ops.body:
**Third suite, 2026-08-30 — the family is growing, and it is now unambiguously the assertion style rather than any one suite.**

`SnapshotWatcherTests.watchesDirectoryAcrossAtomicRename()` failed on daemonkit CI run **33289395786**, commit `dc3816a`, job `swift`:

```
✘ Test watchesDirectoryAcrossAtomicRename() recorded an issue at
  SnapshotWatcherTests.swift:245:6: Caught error: WaitTimeout()
✘ Test watchesDirectoryAcrossAtomicRename() failed after 3.840 seconds with 1 issue.
✘ Test run with 70 tests in 16 suites failed after 3.841 seconds with 1 issue.
```

**Same mechanism, new file.** `Tests/DaemonKitTests/SnapshotWatcherTests.swift:72-81` defines `waitUntil(_ seconds: Double = 3, …)`, which polls a condition against a fixed 3-second `ContinuousClock` deadline and throws `WaitTimeout()` on expiry. Here the condition is an FS-watch callback observing an atomic rename — the `debounce: 0.05` window plus `DispatchSource`/kqueue delivery simply did not land inside a 3s wall-clock budget on a loaded hosted runner.

That makes **three** distinct suites in this family:

| Suite | Assertion shape |
|---|---|
| `ServiceSocketClientDeadlineTests` | fixed wall-clock deadlines (`< 0.15s` bound, 5s readiness budget) |
| `SessionReadinessTests` | fixed readiness margins (`>= .milliseconds(40)` against 0.05s literals) |
| **`SnapshotWatcherTests`** | **`waitUntil` fixed 3s poll budget racing FS-event delivery** |

**Not a regression — ruled out rather than assumed.** `dc3816a` is a Go-only de-cruft sweep (`internal/proc/legacy_bbolt.go`, `deploy/record.go`, `stop.go`, `docs/MIGRATING-0.21.md`, dropping `go.etcd.io/bbolt`). It touched **no** file under `Sources/` or `Tests/`, and nothing in the `SnapshotWatcher` debounce/kqueue path. Every other workflow on that commit passed — Fleet build 14/14, Mixed era, Export census, Docs drift, Guides, cc-notes — and the other 69 Swift tests in this very run passed, **including both suites already named in this task**. Triaged before re-running rather than reflexively hitting retry.

## Why the third instance changes the recommendation

With one suite this reads as a flaky test. With three independent suites failing the same way, the defect is the **shared idiom**: a literal wall-clock budget asserted against work whose latency is set by runner scheduling, FS-event delivery, and socket readiness — none of which the test controls. Each new suite that adopts `waitUntil`-with-a-default inherits the flake for free, which is exactly how this spread from one file to three.

So the fix is structural, not per-test: drive these off an **injectable clock** or a measured baseline, the way the Go side's `wiretest` harness advances a clock manually instead of sleeping. Patching individual literals upward buys time and guarantees a fourth suite later.

## And it is still a release blocker

`release.yml` calls `require_workflow CI`, so any one of these three going red stops a tag being cut, with re-running until it wins as the only remedy. Tonight that cost a triage cycle on a green change. The standing rule in this fleet is that a gate which red-lights clean pushes trains people to re-run without reading — which is precisely how 18,999 handshake failures once stayed invisible behind green CI.
